adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent the new fallback logic is:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined, the `find` compares each `cal.externalId` to that same falsy value, so it will almost never match and `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined` even when `event.destinationCalendar` contains a valid externalId. Unlike `createEvent`, there is no `|| "primary"` fallback here, so the subsequent `calendar.events.update({ calendarId: selectedCalendar, ... })` will pass an undefined `calendarId`, which is a real correctness bug introduced by this diff.
